classification.difficultyReason: Coordinate two binomial models and enumerate complementary success counts, with the five-case strategy explicitly supplied.

content.prompt: A man is restoring ten old cars, six of them manufactured in 1955 and four of them manufactured in 1962. When he tries to start them, on average the 1955 models will start 65% of the time and the 1962 models will start 80% of the time. Assume the cars start independently. Find, correct to four decimal places, the probability that at any time:

children.label: a
children.prompt: exactly three of the 1955 models and one of the 1962 models will start,

answer.worked:
Let $X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(6,0.65)$ count the 1955 cars that start and $Y\sim\operatorname{Bin}(4,0.8)$ count the 1962 cars that start. The variables are independent.
$$\begin{aligned}P(X=3,Y=1)&=\binom63(0.65)^3(0.35)^3\binom41(0.8)(0.2)^3\\&=0.006028568\\&\approx0.0060.\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: exactly four of the cars will start. Consider five cases.

answer.worked:
Let $X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(6,0.65)$ and $Y\sim\operatorname{Bin}(4,0.8)$ independently count the starting cars from 1955 and 1962 respectively. Exactly four cars start in the five cases $(X,Y)=(0,4),(1,3),(2,2),(3,1),(4,0)$.
$$\begin{aligned}P(X+Y=4)&=\sum_{x=0}^{4}\binom6x(0.65)^x(0.35)^{6-x}\binom4{4-x}(0.8)^{4-x}(0.2)^x\\&=0.0007529536+0.0083900544+0.014607684\\&\quad+0.006028568+0.000524808375\\&=0.030304068375\\&\approx0.0303.\end{aligned}$$
